title: Repository SBOM and hierarchy cross-validation audit
scope: Current checkout; generated npm SBOM and source hierarchy, not a user-supplied artifact or built binary
changes: Audit artifacts only; no application source, dependency installations or production data changed in this turn.

limitations: Not a manual review of every repository source file.
No supplied external SBOM, compiled artifact or deployed hierarchy was provided.
No dynamic execution, exploit proof, binary hash verification, complete license text/notice review or live model calls.
XML SBOM import is not supported by current code.

cross_validation.scope: Current checkout; generated npm SBOM and source hierarchy, not a user-supplied artifact or built binary
limitations: npm lockfile inventory only; excludes unlisted ecosystems, vendored code and build artifacts.
Peer/workspace dependency resolution is not inferred; no vulnerability or license compliance verdict.

python.scope: Installed local virtual environment, including development tools; editable local packages excluded

advisory_results.interpretation: Advisory aliases can duplicate the same issue; package matches do not prove application exploitability.

review_candidates: 13 MPL-2.0 entries, including axe-core and lightningcss variants
license_assessment.guidance: Do not infer that repository MIT licensing applies to dependencies or that dev/platform entries ship in production.

new_audit_reproductions.reason: Confirmed unfixed SPDX root and license expression conversion defects

findings.description: Installed cryptography 48.0.1 matches three reviewed advisories; cryptography>=44,<49 excludes all their fixed releases.

evidence.code_use: backend/services/shared_reviews.py:151 uses Fernet; no direct PKCS#7 or x509 verifier usage found in inspected services/core.

findings.root_cause: Upper version cap excludes patched versions; no advisory scan in inspected CI workflow.
findings.impact: Vulnerable distribution installed, but affected API reachability through the application has not been established.
findings.reproduction: Run the approved OSV query script against the current environment and compare affected ranges with installed version.
findings.recommended_fix: Review cryptography 50+ compatibility, update the dependency range, reinstall, re-scan and test encrypted session profile round trips. Do not replace encryption with a workaround.
findings.validation: No remaining matching advisory for selected release; full backend suite and SQLite profile encryption/decryption tests pass.

findings.description: Installed pytest 8.4.2 matches CVE-2025-71176; pytest>=7.4,<9 excludes fixed 9.0.3.

evidence.platform: This machine is Windows; advisory concerns Unix /tmp handling. CI also runs Ubuntu.

findings.root_cause: Development tool cap excludes security release.
findings.impact: Risk to shared Unix development/CI environments; no Windows runtime exploit claimed.
findings.reproduction: Compare installed pytest version and development constraint with advisory range.
findings.recommended_fix: Allow a compatible patched pytest release and validate both CI platforms; use private test temporary directories as defense in depth.
findings.validation: Re-scan selected pytest release; all tests pass on Windows and Linux.

findings.description: SPDX JSON documentDescribes application roots are ignored.
findings.root_cause: Only explicit DESCRIBES/DESCRIBED_BY relationship objects are processed.
findings.impact: A valid document can show unknown roots and no application-to-component lineage even though the root is recorded.
findings.reproduction: Import SPDX 2.3 with packages and documentDescribes=[SPDXRef-App], without redundant relationship objects.
findings.recommended_fix: Union validated documentDescribes references with supported root relationships; reject unknown endpoints.
findings.validation: Root import reproduction passes; approved export retains application-root path; duplicate roots remain idempotent.

findings.description: npm SPDX license expressions are exported as arbitrary license names rather than expressions.
findings.root_cause: All npm license strings are unconditionally placed under license.name.
findings.impact: The original text survives, but downstream license consumers lose structured alternative/conjunction semantics.
findings.reproduction: Generate a BOM from npm package-lock with license=(MIT OR CC0-1.0).
findings.recommended_fix: Validate SPDX IDs/expressions and emit license.id or expression as appropriate; preserve unknown free-form names without claiming verified licensing.
findings.validation: Round-trip MIT, OR, AND, WITH and LicenseRef cases against CycloneDX schema; malformed declarations remain explicit.

findings.description: Generated BOM excludes Python runtime dependencies and their transitives.
findings.root_cause: Generation supports configured npm lockfiles only.
findings.impact: The application-wide supply-chain view omits its backend, including the cryptography advisory matches.
findings.reproduction: Generate current repository inventory and compare it with requirements-local.txt and installer inputs.
findings.recommended_fix: Import or generate an environment/build-specific Python BOM and merge with ecosystem-qualified identities; retain separate runtime/development/optional scopes.
findings.validation: Manifest and installed Python package sets reconcile without hiding unresolved version ranges.

findings.description: Package inventory and source hierarchy are colocated but lack source-import-to-component evidence links.

evidence.source_imports: Regex screening found no undeclared frontend external package names after excluding built-in node:path; not proof of whole-repository completeness.

findings.root_cause: attach adds repository membership and SBOM depends_on edges, without binding source imports to package identities.
findings.impact: Ghost dependencies, per-function package usage and executable reachability cannot be established from the graph.
findings.reproduction: Inspect edges crossing from source-derived resources to sbom_component nodes in generated graph.
findings.recommended_fix: Correlate imports with ecosystem resolver evidence and explicit unresolved states; validate against build output before asserting unused or exploitable packages.
findings.validation: Controlled fixtures cover a declared used dependency, undeclared import, dynamic import and build-only package without false unused verdicts.

findings.description: Generated components omit package URLs and tarball hashes despite lockfile integrity evidence; imported hashes are absent from normalized graph properties.

evidence.qualification: Imported original SBOM document is retained unchanged; evidence is unavailable in graph properties, not deleted from original export.

findings.root_cause: Generated component and normalized component projections omit these fields.
findings.impact: Graph identity correlation and artifact comparison are weaker; this does not prove artifact tampering.
findings.reproduction: Compare generated BOM/normalized graph with lockfile integrity and a CycloneDX component containing SHA-256 hashes.
findings.recommended_fix: Preserve validated hashes and purls; convert supported SRI algorithms correctly and distinguish archive integrity from built-binary integrity.
findings.validation: Known SRI fixture yields exact expected hex hash; imported evidence round-trips to graph and export; no claim of installed-byte verification.

findings.description: Peer relationships are omitted, leaving 18 recorded components unreachable from application roots.

evidence.example: @stencil/react-output-target records required peer @stencil/core; the peer is in the inventory but its edge is omitted.
evidence.qualification: Optional and platform package entries are not proof of unused or malicious dependencies. resolution_complete refers only to attempted dependencies.

findings.root_cause: Dependency iteration includes dependencies and optionalDependencies but not peerDependencies.
findings.impact: Shortest paths and transitive impact are incomplete for peer relationships.
findings.reproduction: Traverse generated depends_on graph from roots; compare unreachable components with package-lock peerDependencies.
findings.recommended_fix: Retain explicit peer relationship types and resolved installation context; report each relationship class coverage separately.
findings.validation: Peer fixtures establish correct direction and nested resolution; unsupported/workspace cases are visibly partial.

remediation_order: SC-01 and SC-02: resolve dependency caps and validate compatibility
SC-03 and SC-04: repair root/license projections with regression tests
SC-07: retain package identity and integrity evidence
SC-05, SC-06 and SC-08: extend ecosystem coverage and correlation only as authorized
approval_history: Initial all-environment Python metadata transmission rejected by automatic approval review; user explicitly approved complete environment lookup, which subsequently completed.

limitations: Package advisory matches do not prove runtime exploitability or license compliance.

remaining_scope: Python/other ecosystem inventory requires imported SBOM
Source imports are not bound to installed package/runtime identities
License compliance is not established by inventory

status_by_finding.SC-02: Dependency range and local installed version updated; Windows suite passed; Linux execution remains CI validation.
status_by_finding.SC-04: Fixed with SPDX expression parser and regression tests.
status_by_finding.SC-05: Remaining scope: import externally generated Python/customer SBOM through managed sbom_path.
status_by_finding.SC-06: Remaining scope: source-to-package/runtime binding not implemented.
status_by_finding.SC-07: Generated purls/SRI hashes and imported checksum evidence retained; actual artifact bytes not verified.
status_by_finding.SC-08: Resolved installation-context peer relationships included; workspace links remain explicit limitation.
